scope: A constructed false expected answer with valid real source quotation is passed through the production v2 critique, then tested against the real bank approval gate. Generation of the negative-control proposal is deterministic, not an actual model output.

objectives.title: Evaporation
objectives: Explain liquid water changing to water vapor.

objectives.title: Condensation
objectives: Explain water vapor changing to liquid water.

source_passages.text: Evaporation changes liquid water into water vapor, a gas. A puddle can shrink as water evaporates into the air. The water has changed state; it has not disappeared.

Condensation changes water vapor into liquid water. When water vapor in air cools near a cold surface, liquid droplets can form on the surface. Evaporation and condensation describe opposite changes of state.

structural_validation.explanation: Question/source/concept identities and exact quotation all validate. Those checks do not prove that the quote supports the false expected answer.

constructed_proposal.prompt_text: Compare a shrinking puddle and droplets on a cold glass. Explain water's starting and ending state in each observation.
constructed_proposal.expected_answer: Evaporation changes water vapor into liquid water. Condensation also changes water vapor into liquid water, so the two processes have the same direction.
answer_criteria: Explain evaporation as water vapor changing into liquid water.
Explain condensation as gas changing to liquid.
constructed_proposal.partial_answer_guidance: Credit an explanation of gas changing to liquid for each observation.

source_support.quote: Evaporation changes liquid water into water vapor, a gas.
source_support.criterion: Explain evaporation as water vapor changing into liquid water.

source_support.quote: Condensation changes water vapor into liquid water.
source_support.criterion: Explain condensation as gas changing to liquid.

issues.explanation: The answer guidance, evaporation criterion, and partial-credit guidance incorrectly treat evaporation in the shrinking puddle as gas changing to liquid. Passage water-01 states that evaporation changes liquid water into water vapor. The guidance also incorrectly says the processes have the same direction; water-02 explicitly describes them as opposite changes. The cited evaporation quote contradicts its attached criterion.

educational_review: The expected answer reverses evaporation and falsely treats the two changes as having the same direction. The cited passage explicitly defines evaporation as liquid-to-gas. This deliberately constructed false answer demonstrates why exact quotations and valid IDs are insufficient; the actual semantic critique caught the contradiction and the server blocked bank approval. One successful negative control does not establish universal semantic reliability.
